note: Hand-picked example ids from results.json (examples[].id = model/task). 'examples' play in the hero story card, in this order; 'pipeline' plays in the How it works walkthrough (runs whose C packet was stored). Only the curation and the plain-language framing live here, with no figures; every answer, verdict, truth and packet is read from results.json at runtime. Each 'why' line describes what that run actually did, checked against its stored final answer.

examples.title: How many steps did I take yesterday?

why.A_raw: Added the phone and the watch together, so every step was counted twice.
why.B_tools: Fetched both devices and reported the combined count from all of them.
why.C_broker: Counted one device per day, so a walk is counted once.

examples.title: How many steps did I take this week?

why.A_raw: Added up the days it had and gave a confident total, though some days had no data.
why.B_tools: Fetched the week, noticed the missing days and answered unknown.
why.C_broker: Said the total cannot be known, because some days have no data.

examples.title: Did I sleep less than usual the last few nights?

why.A_raw: Got this one right by working through the rows.
why.B_tools: Said no, and missed that the last few nights were much shorter.
why.C_broker: Compared the recent nights with the person's own usual range.

examples.title: What was my resting heart rate yesterday?

why.A_raw: Gave a number, but the watch had no reading for yesterday.
why.B_tools: Also gave a number for a day with no reading.
why.C_broker: Saw the watch had not synced lately and said the answer is unknown.

pipeline.title: Missing days
pipeline.why: Some days have no data. Adding up the days that are there gives a confident total that is wrong.

pipeline.title: New watch
pipeline.why: A new device starts a new baseline. Reading the two series as one invents a trend.

pipeline.title: Stale sync
pipeline.why: The watch has not synced lately. No recent nights means the answer is unknown, not no.

pipeline.title: HRV trend
pipeline.why: Night-to-night wobble reads as a slide. A fixed trend test over local days, across a clock change, says steady.

pipeline.title: Steps counted twice
pipeline.why: The phone and the watch both count the same walk. Adding the two sources double-counts.
